newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may not load all soybeans registered-Abiove.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may not load all soybeans registered-Abiove.

text.p: Brazil may not load all the soybeans registered for export so far as some exporters could buy back product to attend to domestic industry demand, said the Brazilian Association of Vegetable Oils Industries (Abiove).
Brazil registered 8.69 million tonnes of soybeans for export by July 31, which represents 102.3 percent of forecast exports of 8.5 million tonnes, Abiove said earlier this week.
The association upwardly revised its forecasts for exports of soymeal and soyoil but left the outlook for soybeans unchanged.

"For beans, even though our forecast has been exceeded, I'm going to leave it (unchanged) for a bit because there could be some buy-back operations," said Fabio Trigueirinho, secretary general of Abiove.
Traders last month reported that various industries, including processor Ceval Alimentos, had bought back product sold earlier in the year.
But Abiove estimated soymeal exports would reach 9.3 million tonnes in the 1997/98 marketing year, which lasts from February to January, up from a previous forecast of 8.9 million tonnes.
Soyoil exports were seen at 1.0 million ones, up from the 850,000 tonnes previously expected. It upped its crushing estimate accordingly to 18.3 million tonnes from 18.0 million tonnes.
Abiove will continue to monitor fortnightly export registration figures from the state export department Secex and will revise its forecasts if needed, Trigueirinho said.
"It will be necessary to revise the forecast for soymeal and soyoil exports a little higher," he predicted.
Brazil exported 3.6 million tonnes of soybeans, 10.8 tmillion tonnes of soymeal and 1.3 million tonnes of soyoil in 1996/97, according to Abiove statistics.
